question: A library has a million books. Why does its catalog, sorted by title, make finding one book fast?
options: It lets you skip straight to the right drawer and card instead of walking every shelf
Cards are smaller than books, so reading every card is quicker than walking every shelf
It keeps the books on the shelves in title order
It holds every detail of each book, so you never need to visit the shelf
explanation: The catalog is an index: a small sorted structure that points to where each book is. Each label narrows the search, so a few steps replace a walk past a million books. Reading every card would still take a million steps, and the catalog neither moves the books nor replaces them. It must be updated when a book arrives.
